newsitem.title: UK: Frontline considers bond issue for VLCCs.
newsitem.headline: Frontline considers bond issue for VLCCs.

text.p: Frontline, the Bermuda-based tanker owner, said on Friday it is considering financing four new VLCCs through a bond issue.
However, the company said it remained committed to the planned secondary listing of its shares in the United States in addition to its current Oslo stock market quote.
It said it is also "considering different strategic alternatives" to increase its size and competitiveness.
Frontline made no direct comment on its previously stated interest in acquiring another listed tanker owner, London & Overseas Freighters Plc
"The board is now seriously considering an issue of a non-amortizable long-term bond financing," Frontline said in a statement.
Frontline said it was one of a number of "several alternatives" for financing options to build four VLCCs at South Korea's Hyundai Heavy Industries.
"The strengthening of the VLCC market and the competitive cash breakeven rates the company has achieved after restructuring has increased the number of alternatives available," Frontline said.
Over $250 million has been raised through bond issues by tanker companies this summer for expansion of their fleets.
Global Ocean Carriers Ltd raised $126 million and B&H Ocean Carriers Ltd subsidiary Equimar Shipholdings Ltd raised a further $125 million.
Frontline said shareholders had approved board proposals to increase the share capital by 10 million shares at NOK 28.15 each.
The shares were bought by four major institutional investors in a private placement executed on 14 July.
The cash raised was used to exercise options to build three suezmax tankers at Hyundai, due for delivery between June and August 1998.
